newsitem.title: UK: LME copper snaps above $2,200, ends firmer.
newsitem.headline: LME copper snaps above $2,200, ends firmer.

text.p: Copper prices snapped back above the $2,200 level during late-afternoon LME trading on Wednesday, and prices concluded a mostly low-key session firmer.

Traders said the late gains reflected the routine Dec option expiry earlier. This removed some of the volatility and uncertainty from the market as the large open interest calls remained out-of-the-money and thus passed out of the picture.

"After all the horror stories about blood on the streets it was your typical LME option expiry. A strike was at-the-money and there were partial declarations. Once it was out of the way,there was a little bit of fresh buying this afternoon," one said.
The strike at which attention focussed was $2,300, but open interest was manageable, and hedging had been concluded well before expiry.

The underlying market traded comfortably throughout, and apart from towards the close was rangebound under $2,200. In the short-term, stock movements and "third Wednesday" tightness will dictate direction now, traders said.
Last three months business was at $2,208 a tonne, up $25 from Tuesday's kerb. Spread backwardations held steady throughout, with cash/threes ending at $170.

There was also little excitement at option declaration in aluminium, with calls at $1,500 declared and puts abandoned. But the forward market built on recent technical consolidation and physical interest to push higher.
Profit-taking stemmed gains at $1,540, but final business was at $1,537, up $10 from Tuesday.
Nickel prices made consistent if unspectacular progress throughout the session, with the market's short-term technical objective pegged at $7,000. Last kerb business was at $6,945, up $110.
Lead prices staged a mini-rally during the afternoon kerb, erasing early losses, and last trade was at $688, up $2.

Zinc was inhibited to some extent by Tuesday's stock increase, although the overall fundamental and technical picture remains bright. Prices closed the kerb at $1,069, up $8 from Tuesday, aided by support around $1,060 this morning.
Tin hardly moved throughout most of a slow session before snapping above $6,100 during the late kerb. Three months closed at $6,115, against a previous finish of $6,080.
Alloy was assisted by the trend in primary metal, and ended at a steadier $1,368/73 a tonne.
